theme: भय, प्रतिष्ठा, और कर्तव्य का नैतिक परीक्षण / Fear, honor, and the moral test of duty
context: Krishna now sharpens the social and moral consequence of Arjuna’s withdrawal. The issue is not simply whether he feels afraid; it is whether a respected warrior can abandon the field and still keep integrity. Krishna says that the great warriors who admired Arjuna will think he fled from fear, and that public loss of honor will become a deep inner wound.
contextHindi: कृष्ण अब अर्जुन की पीछे हटने की स्थिति का सामाजिक और नैतिक परिणाम और स्पष्ट करते हैं। बात केवल यह नहीं है कि अर्जुन डर रहा है; सवाल यह है कि एक सम्मानित योद्धा अगर युद्ध छोड़ दे, तो उसकी गरिमा और आत्म-सम्मान कैसे बचता है। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो महारथी अर्जुन का सम्मान करते थे, वे समझेंगे कि उसने भय से पीछे हटकर पलायन किया है, और यह अपमान केवल बाहरी नहीं, भीतर का भी घाव बन जाएगा।
sanskritDevanagari:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः |
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ||२-३५||
transliteration:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ .
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam ||2-35||

wordByWord.meaning: From battle, from the field; युद्ध से, रणभूमि से।
Having withdrawn, having ceased; पीछे हटकर, रुककर।
They will think, they will conclude; वे मानेंगे, वे समझेंगे।
Great warriors, highly accomplished fighters; बड़े योद्धा, महारथी।
Highly honored, widely esteemed; बहुत मान्य, बहुत सम्मानित।
Having become, having been; होकर, बनकर।
Lightness, trivialization, cowardly ease; हल्कापन, तुच्छता, भय से पीछे हटना।

spokenHindi:
यह श्लोक एक बहुत सख्त सवाल उठाता है। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि अगर तुम युद्ध से पीछे हट जाओगे, तो वे महारथी, जिनका तुम सम्मान था, सोचेंगे कि तुम भय से भागे हो। यह सिर्फ ‘लोग क्या कहेंगे’ की चिंता नहीं है; यह यह भी बताता है कि एक सम्मानित व्यक्ति अगर अपने कर्तव्य से पीछे हटता है, तो उसका भीतर का मान भी टूटता है।

‘लाघवम्’ का अर्थ है हल्कापन, तुच्छता, या अपने कर्तव्य को छोटा समझकर पीछे हट जाना। यह श्लोक यह नहीं कहता कि समाज की राय सब कुछ है, लेकिन यह बहुत साफ कहता है कि जब आप अपने लिए सही काम को छोड़ते हैं, तो आप सिर्फ बाहरी स्थिति से नहीं बचते—आप अपने भीतर भी अपने को कम समझने लगते हैं।

इसलिए कृष्ण का तात्पर्य यह नहीं है कि सिर्फ प्रतिष्ठा की रक्षा करो। उनका संकेत है कि अगर एक व्यक्ति अपने कर्तव्य को समझता है, तो डर, शोक या भावनात्मक उलझन उसे ‘अच्छा’ बहाना बनाने का मौका नहीं देती। सही कर्तव्य का सवाल केवल ‘क्या मुझे दुख है?’ नहीं है; सवाल यह है, ‘क्या मैं सत्य और जिम्मेदारी के साथ खड़ा हूँ?’
clearEnglish:
Krishna’s point here is neither vanity nor mere social pressure. He is naming a practical moral truth: when a respected person withdraws from a legitimate duty because of fear, others will read that withdrawal as a sign of weakness. The verse is not saying that public opinion is the only measure of worth, but it is saying that a person’s own actions shape how they are seen and how they later experience themselves.

The term lāghavam means lightness, trivialization, or a lowering of one’s own standing. It describes the inner moral cost of treating a serious responsibility as if it were optional or disposable. Krishna is warning Arjuna that the problem is not only the battlefield; it is also the self-judgment that follows when one abandons the role one has been entrusted with. This is not a call to pride, but a call to avoid cowardly self-excuse.

The verse therefore presents a profound ethical test: are we acting from awareness and responsibility, or are we letting fear and emotion shrink our own capacity to stand in truth? In modern life, this applies whenever we avoid a hard but necessary responsibility by calling it compassion, confusion, or self-care without honestly checking whether we are evading what we know is required.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states that if Arjuna withdraws from battle, the great warriors who respected him will think he acted out of fear; thus his honor is diminished and his inner standing is damaged.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Traditional readings emphasize that the question is not simply reputation but the moral consequence of abandoning a duty one has a real responsibility to fulfill.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A reasonable inference is that fear can become a form of self-deception when it is used to excuse refusal without truly examining whether the duty is genuine or the avoidance is merely emotional retreat.

interpretationPerspectives.label: CUSTOM
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: In many communities, honor, family standing, and public reputation strongly shape how duty is experienced. That cultural frame matters, but it does not replace the deeper moral question of whether one is acting truthfully or merely protecting the self from discomfort.

practicalApplication.label: Name the real pressure
practicalApplication.text: Before stepping back from a hard responsibility, ask which fear is speaking: fear of pain, fear of responsibility, or fear of being seen as wrong.

practicalApplication.label: Protect dignity by truth
practicalApplication.text: Choose a truthful action over a comforting excuse; the strongest self-respect is built by acting with clarity, not by hiding behind emotional overwhelm.

reflectionQuestion: When fear makes a duty feel unbearable, how do I separate a genuine moral refusal from a self-protective retreat disguised as compassion?
reflectionQuestionHindi: जब डर किसी कर्तव्य को असहनीय लगा दे, तो मैं कैसे पहचानूँ कि यह सचमुच नैतिक अस्वीकृति है या सिर्फ़ आत्म-रक्षा की छिपी हुई पलायन-भाषा है?
